## Pass 242 — 2026-10-16 — `ACTION UK` IS CLOSED: EMEA AND LATAM ARE MEASURED. AND THE PASS'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING IS NOT A REPO — IT IS THAT **THE EU HAS MOVED THE EDUCATION HIGH-RISK DEADLINE TO `2027-12-02`**, WHICH CHANGES THE SEQUENCING OF EVERY EMEA ENGAGEMENT

🟢 **`21` permissive rows across all four regions plus Global, every grant read first-hand: EMEA `3`, LATAM `3`, APAC `4`, North America `3`, Global `8`.** 🔴 **`ACTION UP` STANDS UNCHANGED: the `$6.4`–`11.4` B spread *(`78`%, three firms)* recorded at `p238` is still the only honest statement of market size on these shelves, and quoting a point estimate from here is still forbidden.** 🔵 **No new market figure is introduced by this pass — the regional legs returned REGULATORY and ADOPTION evidence, not sizing, and that is recorded as what it is.**

🔵 **Evidence:** [`p242-verified-rows`](../evidence/p242-verified-rows.2026-10-16-p242.tsv) · [`p242-withheld`](../evidence/p242-withheld.2026-10-16-p242.tsv) · [`p242-websearch`](../evidence/p242-websearch.2026-10-16-p242.tsv) · [`p242-axis-rediscovery`](../evidence/p242-axis-rediscovery.2026-10-16-p242.tsv)

### 🔴 `T242-F` — the EMEA timeline has MOVED, and these shelves were carrying the old one

🔴 **The EU's Digital Omnibus on AI postpones the Annex III high-risk obligations — the tier that contains education — from the 2026 dates to `2027-12-02`, with high-risk AI embedded in regulated products moving to `2028-08-02`.** Council final sign-off reported at `2026-06-29`.

🟡 **Reported with its uncertainty, because the sources disagree on firmness:** one guide gives the postponement as settled, another describes the Council's green light as recent, and an earlier update still had it pending. 🔵 **The Official Journal is the primary source and this pass did not read it.** 🔴 **`ACTION WF`: verify the Annex III date against the Official Journal text before any client-facing use.**

🟢 **What is NOT postponed, and matters more for sequencing:**

- 🔴 **The prohibition on emotion recognition in schools is already in force** *(from `2025-02-02`, subject to the medical/safety exception)*. A proctoring or engagement-detection feature is not a 2027 problem.
- 🔴 **The Article 4 AI-literacy duty already applies to staff who use AI.** That is a training and documentation obligation live today.
- 🔵 **Scope is extraterritorial**: any provider placing an AI product on the EU market, or deploying one affecting EU learners, is in scope regardless of where it is headquartered.

🟡 **The commercial reading, stated plainly: the delay moves the COMPLIANCE ARTEFACT deadline, not the PROHIBITIONS, and it lengthens the window in which a European institution can pilot.** 🔵 **Independently corroborated from the supply side:** this pass's harvest surfaced [`matteoangeloni-jpeg/-NO-AI-ACT`](https://github.com/matteoangeloni-jpeg/-NO-AI-ACT), an Italian browser serious-game on the AI Act whose own description says *"aggiornato al Digital Omnibus"* — 🔴 withheld on `GPL-3.0`, but it is a second, independent signal that the Omnibus is what the European education market is currently reading.

🔴 **And the demand side is not ready:** the **European Schools** have approved **no** generative-AI tool for system-wide use, and their assessment procedure for AI tools is still under development.

### 🔵 Market sizing — the discipline, restated because it keeps being tested

🔴 **`ACTION UP` holds.** Three firms' 2026 education-AI estimates span `$6.4`–`11.4` B, a `78`% spread. 🔵 **A spread that wide is not a market size; it is a disagreement about what to count.** 🟡 **No figure in this pass's regional legs is a sizing figure, and none has been promoted into one.** The one adoption number below is reported as a survey result with its own internal contradiction attached.

## Opportunities by region

🔵 *Pass 242 · 2026-10-16. One subsection per region, all five present. A region with nothing found says so rather than being omitted.*

### North America

🔵 **The buyer is the district, and `2026` is the year the mandates landed with dates on them.** Measured this pass: `~100` state bills tracked in the 2026 session; `33`–`35` states plus Puerto Rico now carry official K-12 AI guidance.

| jurisdiction | the binding thing | when |
|---|---|---|
| **Ohio** | districts **must** have adopted an AI policy; a state model policy was issued | 🔴 `2026-07-01` — **already passed** |
| **Maryland** | `SB 720` *(Ch. 634)*: every local school system **must designate a non-instructional central-office AI coordinator** | signed `2026-05-26` |
| **Tennessee** | local boards must implement student/faculty/staff AI-use policies | enacted 2024 |
| **Oklahoma** | `SB 1734`: written district AI policy | before the `2027`–`28` school year 🟡 *(timing reported inconsistently)* |
| **Utah** | model policies, local adoption, public process, training, parent comms, review | local deadline `Jul 2027` |
| **Idaho** | `SB 1227` **prohibits AI replacing human teachers** | enacted |

🟢 **The opportunity, specifically: Maryland has created a NAMED ROLE in every district and given it no tooling.** 🔵 A central-office AI coordinator has to inventory tools, run a disclosure process and evidence it — which is exactly `p241`'s compliance-and-records stack *(`state-ai-disclosure-state-tracker`, `student-data-access-audit-stream`, `ferpa-haystack`)*, now with a statutory buyer attached. 🟡 **And `p242` adds the parent-facing half**: [`noestudios/lastbell`](https://github.com/noestudios/lastbell) *(`MIT`)* is the first row on these shelves built for the **family** side of the ParentVUE/Canvas record, which is where Utah's and Florida's parent-communication requirements land.

🔴 **Conflict recorded, not resolved:** one tracker reports Colorado repealed its AI Act in `May 2026` while another still lists it as covering educational AI as high-risk. 🟡 **Do not cite Colorado either way from these shelves.**

### EMEA

🔵 **The regulatory picture is `T242-F` above: Annex III high-risk moved to `2027-12-02`, prohibitions and AI-literacy duties live now, extraterritorial scope.**

🟢 **The supply picture, measured for the first time since `p240`:** the permissive EMEA rows are **adapters to national incumbents**, not platforms —

- [`krzysztofbury/librus-python-api`](https://github.com/krzysztofbury/librus-python-api) *(`MIT`)* fronts **Librus Synergia**, the Polish national gradebook, and carries a **weekly live-check CI** against the real upstream.
- [`CarlSvejstrup/dtu-learn-mcp`](https://github.com/CarlSvejstrup/dtu-learn-mcp) *(`MIT`)* fronts **DTU Learn** plus Panopto transcripts at a named Danish university.

🟡 **So the EMEA opportunity is integration into a NATIONAL system of record, under a regime whose artefact deadline just moved out by a year** — and the sovereignty preference is visible in the rows themselves *(`jules` offering Mistral; both adapters running against institution-local systems; `Ollama` as the default in three of this pass's EMEA/LATAM rows)*.

🔴 **The EMEA structural blocker `p240` measured has NOT changed:** the richest European education supply is Moodle plugins and they are `16`/`16` `GPL-3.0`. 🟢 **What `p242` adds is the way around it** — `T242-E` in [`verticals/solutions.md`](../verticals/solutions.md): **beside the host, not inside it.** A plugin inherits `GPL-3.0`; an MCP server or API client against the same platform does not.

### LATAM

🔵 **Regulatory map, measured this pass:** education is **largely unregulated across the region**, with AI tools entering classrooms ahead of guidance.

| country | status |
|---|---|
| **Peru** | 🟢 `Ley N° 31814` *(published `2023-07-05`)* — **the only ENACTED national AI statute in Latin America** |
| **Brazil** | `PL 2338/2023` passed the Senate `2024-12-10`, still in the Chamber of Deputies; vote expected **after the October 2026 elections**. 🔴 **Education IS in its high-risk tier** *(impact assessments, human oversight, documentation)*. Separately, the **Digital ECA** *(Law `15.211/2025`)* is in force since `2026-03-17` — age verification and limits for minors; not an AI law but it binds any product with minor users |
| **Chile** | bill `16821-19` introduced `2024-05-07`, in committee. Data-protection law `21.719` was due `2026-12-01`; the executive has proposed moving it to `2027-12-01` |
| **Mexico** | 🔴 **DISPUTED and NOT RESOLVED.** One 2026 guide asserts binding AI obligations enacted in 2026; another says bills exist but none passed. 🟡 **Do not cite Mexico from these shelves** |
| **Regional** | ECLAC 2024 Digital Agenda, endorsed by all 33 member countries — coordination and cross-border capacity building, not binding rules |

🟢 **The supply picture is the strongest LATAM showing these shelves have carried:**

- [`guillermoscript/lms-front`](https://github.com/guillermoscript/lms-front) *(`MIT`, **`40`★**)* — self-declared *"built for LATAM"*, and **it ships the revenue split** *(Stripe Connect platform fee)* plus Supabase RLS. 🟢 **The two things a studio otherwise hand-builds on a LATAM course-marketplace engagement are already in it.**
- [`Dillax/Di-rio-de-Classe-Avalia-es-`](https://github.com/Dillax/Di-rio-de-Classe-Avalia-es-) *(`MIT`)* — a Brazilian teacher's gradebook that is **offline-first and serverless by construction**: no server, data only in the device's IndexedDB.
- [`arvoreeducacao/seedling`](https://github.com/arvoreeducacao/seedling) *(`Apache-2.0`)* — a Brazilian edtech's own sandboxed-execution tool, open-sourced. 🟡 Hiring, not courseware — but a usable sandbox primitive.

🟡 **The opportunity, specifically: Brazil's high-risk tier names education and its vote is deferred past October 2026, while the Digital ECA already binds anything with minor users.** 🔵 So a Brazilian engagement has a **live** obligation *(ECA: age verification, minors' limits)* and a **pending** one *(PL 2338: impact assessment, human oversight)* — and the `MIT` offline-first gradebook row above is the architecture that satisfies the first almost by accident, because no student record leaves the device.

### APAC

🔴 **The pass's most contrarian datapoint, and it is reported with its contradiction intact.** A higher-education global survey finds APAC faculty **the most optimistic** of any region — `57`% say they are excited about AI — while faculty **intent to use** AI **fell `9` points, from `76`% (2025) to `67`% (2026), the LOWEST future-adoption intent of any region.**

🟡 **Those two findings point in opposite directions and this KB does not reconcile them.** 🔵 **The honest reading is that enthusiasm and intent have decoupled in APAC**, which is what a pilot-fatigue pattern looks like — but one survey is not evidence of a cause, and it is logged as a number to watch, not a trend.

🟢 **Other APAC evidence:** South Korea is expanding AI language tools alongside support for foreign families; Japan is moving to **official digital textbooks** and student-led school design.

🔴 **DECLARED GAP, searched and not found: `ACTION WB`.** 🔴 **These shelves have NO source on national AI-in-education rules or school adoption rates for INDIA or CHINA.** The APAC leg ran and returned nothing for either — which matters because they are the two largest education systems on earth, and because this pass published **four** APAC supply rows *(two Chinese, two Indian)* whose regulatory context is therefore unknown. 🟡 **Recorded as an unrun primary-source leg in local-language government sources, NOT as an absence of regulation.**

🟢 **Supply:** the Chinese rows are **self-hostable and serverless** *(`Cloud-Score` on Cloudflare Pages + private R2; `overachievers` as single-file SQLite onto a home NAS)* and the Indian rows are **hackathon-origin and exam-shaped** *(`eduagent` from AgentathonX; `ATLAS` profiling JEE/GATE)*. 🔵 **Two different buyers: in China an individual teacher or parent who wants no server; in India a volume-exam market.**

### Global *(rows that could not be placed, recorded as such)*

🔵 **`8` of `21` rows carry NO regional evidence and are recorded Global with the reason** — `p240`'s rule kept. 🟡 **That is `38`% of the pass unplaced, which is itself the finding:** the agent/tutor layer is region-free because a tutor need not encode a jurisdiction, while **a gradebook must** *(see [`repos/trending.md`](../repos/trending.md))*. 🔵 **A studio asking "what do we already have for region X" should therefore look at the record layer, not the tutor layer.**

🟢 Highest-star Global rows: [`igweze/fobrain`](https://github.com/igweze/fobrain) `Apache-2.0` `10`★ *(full K-12 school management, 100+ modules)*, [`HeliumEdu/platform`](https://github.com/HeliumEdu/platform) `Apache-2.0` `9`★, [`arshawnarbabi/Cogni`](https://github.com/arshawnarbabi/Cogni) `MIT` `6`★.

### 🔴 What this pass says commercially, in three lines

- 🟢 **The reusable layer has moved again.** `p241` found it in compliance and records; `p242` finds it in **the system of record itself** — attendance, gradebook, transcript — and that is the layer where a row is forced to name its jurisdiction.
- 🔴 **Every permissive record-layer row is `0`–`10`★ against `GPL-2.0` incumbents at `345`–`646`★.** The permissive SIS layer is early and unwon. **Starting points for a build, not products to resell.**
- 🟢 **The licence architecture is the sellable insight:** inside a copyleft host the host's terms govern the deliverable; **beside** it, over an API, the studio's terms do. `7` of `8` rows in this pass's LMS-MCP cluster are permissive surfaces over copyleft or proprietary hosts, and **the single `GPL-3.0` exception is the one that is a plugin.**

### 🔴 `T241-H` — a relicensing event, and it is the most commercially consequential row of the pass

🔴 **[`snflwr-ai/snflwr.ai`](https://github.com/snflwr-ai/snflwr.ai) — a K-12 safe AI tutoring platform *(offline, backend-enforced content filtering, parental oversight)* — went `AGPL-3.0` → PROPRIETARY on `2026-09-18`.** Read first-hand from its own `LICENSE`, `2 833` B, `main` · `7feea47e4759`:

> *"This software was published under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3, from `2026-02-27` until `2026-09-18`. This license does not and cannot revoke that grant. Any copy obtained while the AGPL-3.0 license was in effect remains governed by AGPL-3.0 for that copy, and the rights it conferred on its recipients are perpetual."*

🟢 **The notice is unusually honest** — it states the limit of its own effect rather than pretending to revoke. 🔵 **The commercial reading, stated plainly:**

- 🔴 **A studio starting today cannot use it.** The grant after `2026-09-18` is proprietary, and `commercial_use_ok` now correctly returns `RESTRICTED`.
- 🟡 **A fork taken between `2026-02-27` and `2026-09-18` is `AGPL-3.0` forever**, by the licensor's own written acknowledgement. If a client already has one, that is a live `AGPL-3.0` asset with network-copyleft obligations — a due-diligence question, not a dead end.
- 🔵 **It is a datapoint about the category, not one repo.** An offline K-12 tutor with parental controls is the exact shape the US district market is procuring, and its author concluded the open grant was not how to capture that. 🟡 **`ACTION VU`: sweep these shelves' K-12 tutor rows for further relicensing, keying on a `LICENSE` payload that names two licences and a date.**

### 🔵 What this pass says about the US supply, commercially

- 🟢 **The reusable NA rows are all in the layer UNDER the learning product**: a 50-state privacy-regime tracker, a student-records audit stream, an identity-scoped RAG pre-filter, a records de-duplication pipeline, a hackathon session kit. 🔵 **Not one is a tutor or an LMS.**
- 🔴 **The statute vocabulary is exhausted as a discovery axis**: `topic:ferpa` returned `35`% already-carried rows. 🟢 **The product vocabulary is not**: `topic:k12 topic:ai` returned `12` of `12` on-topic at `12` distinct owners.
- 🟡 **And the sellable thing is the same as `p240` found for the GPL estate, arriving by a different route**: the US permissive supply clusters in **compliance, records and procurement plumbing**, which is service work and integration work, not a product a studio resells.

### 🟢 `T238-F` — `ACTION UQ`, and the finding is about the ACTION REGISTER rather than the law

`p236` closed with: *"The EU AI Act high-risk conformity deadline **does not reconcile** — Dec 2027 vs Aug 2028, and sources disagree on whether the Digital Omnibus is in force or merely approved. `ACTION UQ`: resolve against EUR-Lex. **No EMEA proposal should quote a date from these shelves until it is.**"*

🔴 **That action should never have been registered.** `p223` and `p224` — **dated `2026-10-15`, one day earlier** — had already settled every limb of it, and the cells are still on [`agents/trending.md`](../agents/trending.md) in their fifth reproduction:

| limb `p236` reported unresolved | 🟢 what `p223`/`p224` had already published |
|---|---|
| *"Dec 2027 **vs** Aug 2028"* | 🟢 **Not rival dates for one deadline. Two different annexes.** Annex III *(stand-alone, **education is point `3`**)* → **`2027-12-02`**. Annex I *(embedded in regulated products)* → **`2028-08-02`** |
| *"in force or merely approved"* | 🟢 **In force.** `Reg. (EU) 2026/1744`, `OJ` `2026-07-24`, in force `2026-07-27`. Parliament endorsed `2026-06-16`, Council final approval `2026-06-29` |
| *"no EMEA proposal should quote a date"* | 🔴 **An embargo on this KB's own correct answer.** The shelves were right; the register told readers not to trust them |

🔵 **This is `p226`/`p227`'s defect class, inverted: there the gate could not see what the KB had refuted; here the ACTION REGISTER could not see what the KB had ESTABLISHED, so a settled question was re-opened as a gap one pass later.** 🟡 **`ACTION VF`: before registering any action of the form *"resolve X"*, run `make claims TOKEN=X`. The claims gate already answers it and it was not consulted.**

🟢 **This pass re-derived the dates on an independent channel and changed nothing** — `Cuatrecasas`, `White & Case`, `ERTICO`, `NHI Governance`, `nicfab`, the Cloud Security Alliance and `skillsintelligence` all converge on `Reg. (EU) 2026/1744` / `OJ 2026-07-24` / in force `2026-07-27`. 🔴 **`eur-lex.europa.eu` remains unreadable from this session, so the status stays `CONVERGENT-SECONDARY` and `ACTION RO` stands** — see `T238-H` for a refinement of *why* it is unreadable.

🟢 **Two clauses ARE new, and both matter commercially** *(`0` prior occurrences on these shelves)*:

1. 🟢 **The Omnibus moved four application dates and did nothing else.** No obligation added, none removed, **and no sector or company-size exemption.** 🔵 **So the deferral bought time, not relief, and there is no education carve-out and no SME carve-out to hope for.** A client told *"the deadline moved"* who hears *"the rule got softer"* has been misinformed by the summary, not by the law.
2. 🟢 **National regulatory sandboxes must be operational by `2027-08-02`**, four months before education's own date. 🟡 A sandbox place is a deliverable with an earlier clock than the obligation it de-risks.

🔵 **And the nearest genuinely binding EU date is unchanged from `p224`: `2026-12-02`** — the two Article `5` prohibitions the Omnibus added, plus the end of the Article `50(2)` machine-readable marking grace for systems placed before `2026-08-02`. **Seven weeks out.**

## Opportunities by region

### North America

🟢 **The opening is regulatory fragmentation at the state level.** `134` AI-in-education bills were introduced across `31` states in 2026 — data privacy, classroom-use limits, curriculum. Named instruments: **California AB 1159** *(bars using student data to train AI models)*; **Oklahoma** and **Maryland** *(require human oversight; bar AI from high-stakes decisions about students)*; **New York City** *(one-year moratorium on student-facing AI through 8th grade)*. Federal: the **K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 (H.R. 8747)** advanced out of committee `2026-07-21`. Canada's **"AI for All"** strategy (June 2026) is direction, not binding law. Mexico has bills pending and no regulator.

🟢 **The concrete 2026 opening is the Classroom migration**, and it is North-America-weighted because the CS-course estate on GitHub Classroom is. 🔴 **It is time-boxed and already past its deadline**: the platform went dark `2026-08-28` and LTI rosters are reported deleted. 🟢 **Sellable as a fixed-scope engagement**: audit `.github/workflows/` for `classroom-resources/autograding` references, fork the archived `MIT` reporter, stand up a replacement. 🔴 **Price the licence choice explicitly** — `classroom50` is `GPL-3.0`.

🟡 **A `50`-state student-authored framework ("STUDENTS FIRST Act of 2026", AASA, `2026-08-03`) exists** and is a credible stakeholder artefact for public-sector bids.

### EMEA

🔴 **The binding instrument is the EU AI Act, and education is explicitly high-risk** where AI determines access to education or scores exams. 🟢 **Enforcement by the AI Office and national authorities began `2026-08-02`.** 🟢 **Article 4's AI-literacy obligation has applied since `2025-02-02` to every organisation using AI systems — which is every school, now.** 🔴 **Emotion recognition in educational institutions is a prohibited practice** outside medical and safety purposes, and that prohibition is already live.

🔴 **The high-risk conformity deadline does NOT reconcile across sources and this pass refuses to pick one.** The Digital Omnibus on AI moved it; one source says August 2026 → **December 2027**, another gives **`2027-12-02`** for stand-alone high-risk systems and **`2028-08-02`** for those embedded in regulated products; sources also disagree on whether the Omnibus entered into force mid-July 2026 or was merely approved by Council on `2026-06-29` pending Official Journal publication. 🟡 **`ACTION UQ`: resolve against EUR-Lex directly; no EMEA proposal should quote a conformity date from these shelves until it is.**

🟢 **The opportunity is unambiguous even while the date is not**: exam-scoring and admissions systems are high-risk, the literacy duty is already in force, and extraterritorial reach means non-EU vendors serving EU learners are in scope. **Conformity tooling — documentation, logging, human-oversight design, literacy programmes — is billable now.**

### APAC

🟢 **South Korea's AI Basic Act has applied since `2026-01-22`, and its "high-impact" category covers education.** 🔴 **And the region's flagship education-AI programme failed in public**: the Korean AI-textbook rollout saw adoption reported below `30`% and the National Assembly stripped the textbooks' official status. 🔵 **That is the most useful single fact on this shelf for an APAC pitch — the cautionary precedent is domestic, recent, and everyone in the room will know it.** Sell adoption and teacher workflow, not content supply.

🟢 **China is the rollout leader and regulates by service type** — recommendation algorithms, deep synthesis, generative AI, labelling. **AI is a compulsory subject from age six, with Beijing mandating ≥8 hours of AI instruction a year.** 🟢 **Japan's AI Promotion Act carries no penalties**; a new **AI Basic Plan** was adopted July 2026. 🟡 **India has no dedicated AI law**; in July 2026 the government signalled risk-based legislation, alongside a ten-million-teacher training push. 🟢 **Adoption ranking**: Singapore leads, with Australia, Korea and Taiwan close behind; Japan, India and China are relative laggards for different reasons.

🟢 **Supply, measured properly for the first time this pass:** `ACTION UL`'s Japanese and Korean queries found `9` uncarried live repositories. 🔴 **`7` of the `9` carry no licence at all.** 🔵 **So the APAC constraint is not absence of software, it is absence of grants — which is a different and much more tractable engagement problem**: the code exists and its authors are reachable.

### LATAM

🟢 **`p235`'s correction stands and is reinforced: LATAM supply is not zero** — `15` live repositories, `9` permissive, plus three `MIT` Brazilian packages on `PyPI`/`npm`. 🟢 **And demand remains the highest measured of any region** *(Brazil `56%` / Chile `55%` of secondary teachers vs `36%` OECD; `87%` of institutions using AI against `26%` holding a strategy)*.

🟢 **New this pass — the first classroom-specific statute found in the region.** 🔴 **Estado de México reformed article 61 of its state education law in April 2026** to promote responsible, graduated AI use in upper-secondary and higher education — reported as **the first Mexican state to legislate AI in the classroom**. 🟡 **Source is a specialist blog, not the state official gazette; `ACTION UR`: confirm against the Gaceta del Gobierno del Estado de México before it is quoted to a client.**

🟡 **Elsewhere the picture is pending, not absent:** Brazil's **PL 2338/2023** passed the Senate (Dec 2024) and awaits the Chamber of Deputies; Chile's AI bill is in second constitutional reading, with **Ley 21.719** on personal data *(automated profiling and algorithmic decisions)* reported as entering force **`2026-12-01`** — 🔴 **sources conflict on whether it already applies**; Mexico closed its legislative period with no general AI law, leaving sectoral patches. 🔴 **There is no unified Latin American framework for AI in higher education** — stated by an academic source, and that is the gap a regional studio can occupy: **the 87%/26% strategy gap plus `Ley 21.719`'s December date is a concrete, dated reason for a Chilean institution to buy a governance engagement in Q4 2026.**

#### LATAM

🟢 **The strongest position on these shelves, and now with a named supply chain.** Adoption is the highest measured anywhere **`87%`**/`74%`, strategy coverage the lowest **`26%`**: institutions need governance, measurement and integration, not greenfield models. 🟢 **Three concrete entry points, all permissive and all verified this pass:** the **BNCC curriculum layer** *(`@bncc/mcp` + `bncc-dados`)* for alignment and content tagging; **`bncc-benchmark`** *(`15 300` answers, `17` models)* as the ready-made evidence instrument for *"is it accurate on OUR curriculum"*; and **`educabR`/INEP** for the analytics baseline. 🔴 **The three most engagement-shaped artefacts — an ENEM essay grader, a Brazilian dropout study and a Colombian primary-dropout model — are all UNLICENSED**, which is a `1`-file ask away from usable and is `ACTION UJ`. 🔴 **`i-educar` is `GPL-2.0`: integrate beside it, do not build plugins into it without a licence decision.**

### 🟢 `M234-2` — the asymmetry worth stating in one line, because it is the regional strategy

🔴 **LATAM has the highest adoption and the lowest supply. EMEA has the strictest regulation and, as of this pass, the best permissive supply. North America has the most mature standards estate. APAC has the sharpest new regulation and almost no supply.**

🟢 **So the four regions want four different first conversations, and only one of them is about a platform:**

- **EMEA →** *"here is a permissive base you can own, and here is your Article-6 high-risk evidence pack."*
- **LATAM →** *"your teachers and students already adopted this; you have no strategy. Start there."*
- **North America →** *"make 'conformant' auditable."*
- **APAC →** *"your assessment pipeline is now a regulated artefact in at least two jurisdictions."*

## Opportunities by region

### North America

🟢 **The conformance play, unchanged and still the strongest-evidenced.** Ed-Fi is the only `Apache-2.0` platform-scale estate in the region *(`9` repositories, grants read, plus `Ed-Fi-Exchange-OSS/DMS-pilot-testing-kit` — an executable `PASS`/`FAIL` acceptance gate)*. 🔵 **Scope to the target version first: `v7.x` is ODS/API *(admin via `ODS-Admin-API`)*, `v8+` is the Data Management Service.**

🔴 **The regulatory surface is now the differentiator, and it is state-level, not federal.** `134` bills across `31` states this session. **California `AB 1159`** restricts using student data to train AI models. **Oklahoma and Maryland** require human oversight and bar AI from high-stakes decisions about students. **New York City** has a one-year moratorium on student-facing AI through eighth grade. Federally, `H.R. 8747` *(K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026)* passed committee largely along party lines. **Canada's "AI for All"** *(`4 Jun 2026`)* adds a national AI-literacy push, watermarking of AI-generated content and a Canada Trusted AI Certification — 🟡 **not binding law.** **Mexico** has bills but no enforcing regulator.

🟢 **The sellable artefact: a per-state deployment matrix.** *"Human oversight required"* and *"no AI in high-stakes student decisions"* are **engineering requirements**, and a district buying an AI layer cannot answer them from a vendor datasheet. 🔵 **Build it once on the `lti-tool` + Ed-Fi rows and it re-sells `31` times.**

### EMEA

🟢 **This region changed this pass. It now has supply.** Two permissive platform bases, both grant-read:

- 🟢 **`svws-nrw/SVWS-Server`** — `BSD-3-Clause`, a working state SIS, `17` Maven artefacts, an `svws-openapi` seam, and — rarest of all — a `BSD-3-Clause` **anonymised test-database corpus** *(`SVWS-TestSqlites`)* to develop against.
- 🟢 **`openolat/OpenOLAT`** — `Apache-2.0`, a full LMS, `31 854` commits, Swiss-maintained.

🔴 **The regulation is the sharpest in the world and it lands exactly on education's core functions.** The EU AI Act classifies **admissions, student evaluation and exam scoring as high-risk**, and it reaches **non-EU systems whose outputs affect EU students** — so a North American vendor's scoring model is in scope. 🟡 **The dates are UNSETTLED and this KB publishes the conflict rather than resolving it: one source has the AI Office and national authorities enforcing from `2 Aug 2026`; another dates standalone high-risk obligations, education among them, to `2 Dec 2027`; and the Commission's proposed *"AI omnibus"* amendments may move both.** 🔵 **Quote the obligation, not the date — and put the date in a change-control clause.**

🟢 **The combined offer only EMEA supports: FORK + COMPLY.** Fork a permissive base the client owns, and deliver the high-risk evidence pack — human-oversight design, logging, accuracy and bias documentation — against the same codebase. 🔵 **`de.jplag` *(`GPL-3.0`, runs entirely locally, nothing uploaded)* is the academic-integrity engine that survives both GDPR and the Act, precisely because it never leaves the premises.**

### APAC

🔴 **The regulatory hook is the strongest thing in this region, and it is brand new.** **Vietnam's AI law, in force `1 Mar 2026`, names education as a high-risk sector and names automated assessment explicitly** *(compliance for existing systems in 2027 — sources disagree between `1 Mar` and `1 Sep`, and this KB records the disagreement)*. **South Korea's `AI Basic Act` has been in force since `22 Jan 2026`**, risk-based. **Japan** promotes rather than penalises. **China** regulates by service type *(generative AI, content labelling)*. **Australia** relies on technology-neutral law with mandatory guardrails **paused**. **India** has no AI-specific law; its data-protection obligations phase in to May 2027.

🟢 **The pattern worth selling: Vietnam's "automated assessment" and the EU's "exam scoring" are the SAME engineering requirement in two jurisdictions.** 🔵 **One assessment-governance build — provenance, human-in-the-loop sign-off, score logging, appeal trail — satisfies both, and this KB already carries the permissive QTI and LTI rows to wire it to.**

🔴 **Supply is one inferred row.** `HKUDS/DeepTutor` *(`Apache-2.0`, `41.5k` stars, `v1.6.14`)* is the largest permissive education agent on these shelves and its APAC placement rests on an org handle — not on the repository page and not on the grant. 🟡 **`jp.studyplus` is an unprobed lead; `au.edu.` holds one publisher.** 🔴 **Do not represent APAC supply as established. Lead with compliance engineering.**

🟡 **And a demand caveat that should shape the pitch: Ipsos finds `39%` globally think AI should be banned in schools, with Australia and New Zealand HIGHER.** In ANZ, a student-facing AI pitch starts underwater — **lead with teacher-facing workload tools and assessment integrity, not with student chatbots.**

### LATAM

🔴 **Seven passes, three channels, zero supply — and the highest demand of any region.** That is not a gap to apologise for; it is the one place where the shelves' own weakness names the offer.

🟢 **The demand evidence is the best-sourced in this KB** *(TALIS, PISA, UNESCO IESALC — survey instruments, not vendor blogs)*: Brazil `56%` and Chile `55%` of secondary teachers against an OECD average of `36%`; `9` in `10` 15-year-olds across 13 countries using AI chatbots for schoolwork; `87%` of 200 institutions across 19 countries using AI with 🔴 **only `26%` holding a formal AI strategy**; in Brazil, only `22%` of school administrators report their school has AI guidelines.

🔴 **And the equity split is the detail that makes it a design constraint rather than a statistic: in Argentina, usage runs `75%` in higher socio-economic groups against `42%` in lower ones.** 🟢 **So any LATAM deliverable that assumes reliable connectivity encodes that gap into the product.**

🟢 **Three things to sell, in this order:**

1. 🟢 **AI governance as the lead product, not an add-on.** `87%` using against `26%` governed is the arbitrage. UNESCO's regional **Observatory on AI in Education** *(launched `Apr 2026`)*, **Uruguay** *(first LATAM signatory of the Council of Europe AI convention, 2025)* and **Colombia's CONPES 4144** *(Feb 2025)* give an institution external frameworks to anchor a policy to — which is exactly what a `26%` figure says they lack.
2. 🟢 **Offline-first delivery as an equity requirement.** `Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad` *(`Apache-2.0`, Kiwix + Kolibri + Qdrant + local inference, ~`25` GB with the assistant)* is the concrete base. 🔴 **It has NO AUTHENTICATION BY DESIGN — see `P234-R3`, which puts the auth and audit boundary outside it. Never deploy it as-is against student records.**
3. 🟡 **Spanish/Portuguese-language capability as a moat.** The JIME regional assessment found only `7` platforms *(`3.33%`)* offering structured resources under open learning models across Spanish-speaking LATAM. 🔵 **Chamilo and ILIAS are repeatedly described as suited to Spanish-speaking markets and are the realistic integration targets — both copyleft, so INTEGRATE, do not fork.**

🔵 **Stated plainly for a later pass: the absence of LATAM open-source supply is now established on GitHub *(7 passes)*, on package registries *(p232)* and on Maven coordinates *(p234: `mx.` an exact zero)*. It is unlikely to be a measurement artefact. Stop re-measuring it and start selling against it.**

### 🔴 `P227-M2` — South Africa, and why this KB should care more than most

🔴 **South Africa's Draft National AI Policy 2026 was published for comment in April 2026 and then WITHDRAWN — because its reference list cited sources that do not exist.** 🟡 **The two source classes give different withdrawal dates and p227 does NOT pick one:**

| date | source class | reason given |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-06-12` | one secondary source | *"the Draft Policy containing references to non-existent sources"* |

🔵 **A revised version is reportedly due to Cabinet by November 2026, with public release targeted for January 2027. Until then South Africa has no standalone AI statute and AI is governed through POPIA, overseen by the Information Regulator.** 🟢 **The withdrawn draft proposed an AI Ethics Board and an AI Ombudsperson — worth knowing because they are likely to survive into the revision.**

🔴 **The reason this is the pass's most on-point external finding:** 🟢 **a national government published an AI policy whose citations did not resolve, and had to withdraw it. That is precisely the failure these shelves spend every pass defending against, and it is the strongest outside argument yet for the first-hand-read rule and for `ACTION QO`.** 🟡 **The date divergence is the same lesson in miniature: two sources, one event, two dates — and the honest published state is BOTH, with provenance, not an average.**

## Pass 226 — 2026-10-15 — THE TWO REGIMES THAT REGULATE EDUCATION AI BY NAME LAND THEIR OBLIGATIONS IN **LATE 2027**, NOT IN THE `2026` DATE THAT KEEPS CIRCULATING — SO A MULTI-REGION ENGAGEMENT HAS ONE HORIZON AND IT IS TWO YEARS OUT

## Opportunities by region

### 🟢 North America — the regulatory surface is STATE-level and it is now dense enough to be a product

🟢 **`134` AI-in-education bills across `31` states in the `2026` session** — data privacy, classroom-use limits, curriculum integration. Named instruments: **California `AB 1159`** *(bars using student data to train AI models)*, **Idaho `SB 1227`** *(privacy protections for school AI tools)*; **Oklahoma** and **Maryland** require human oversight and bar AI from high-stakes decisions about students. 🔵 **Federal: the `K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026` (`H.R. 8747`) advanced out of the House Education and Workforce Committee at a `July 21` markup.**
🔴 **District-level divergence is the operational risk:** New York City runs a one-year moratorium on student-facing AI through eighth grade; Katy ISD (Texas) bans generative AI chatbots for K-6.
🟢 **The opportunity, stated concretely:** a `50`-state patchwork with a human-oversight requirement recurring across it is a **policy-configuration** problem, not a model problem. 🟡 **A deployment that cannot express *"this district forbids student-facing inference below grade 9"* as configuration will be rebuilt per client.** 🔵 **Market context: North America is reported at `36%` of the AI-in-education market, `USD 3.68B` in 2026 — a vendor-report figure, not verified here.**

### 🟡 EMEA — the obligation is clear, the DATE is the thing clients will get wrong, and the primary source is unreachable from here

🟢 **Consistent across sources: the EU AI Act treats education AI as high-risk where it affects access, assessment or exam scoring — systems that evaluate learners, assign them to programmes, detect prohibited behaviour during assessment, or influence access to qualifications. Those need a conformity assessment before deployment.**
🔴 **The dates returned this pass were mutually inconsistent and at least two were wrong.** 🔴 **`education.ec.europa.eu` — the Commission page this pass's own results named as the one reliable source — is `000` from this pipeline** → [`p226-channel-reachability`](../evidence/p226-channel-reachability.2026-10-15-p226.tsv). 🟡 **So the EMEA date position here is `CONVERGENT-SECONDARY` by necessity, and the settled value stands: `2027-12-02`.**
🟢 **Non-EU EMEA:** the UK runs a principles-based regime rather than a statute; the UAE and Saudi Arabia are both pushing national AI strategies with infrastructure and talent spending; Germany carries a `EUR 20bn` AI investment commitment (`2025-2030`, per one aggregator, unverified).
🟢 **The opportunity:** conformity-assessment evidence is a DELIVERABLE, and almost nothing open-source produces it. 🔵 **A studio that ships the assessment artefacts alongside the system — data provenance, evaluation records, human-oversight design — is selling the part the client cannot buy off the shelf, two years before the deadline.**
🔴 **AFRICA: no African instrument, adoption figure or player was returned under the EMEA query shape. Named as a standing blank, not as coverage** — see the declared blanks below.

### 🟡 APAC — the most fragmented regulatory map, and the only one where a single posture is impossible

🟢 **South Korea** — the `AI Basic Act` *(Framework Act on the Development of AI and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust)* took effect `2026-01-22`; the regulator has signalled `2026` as a pilot year with a one-year penalty grace period. 🟡 **A grace period is a procurement window, not an exemption.**
🟡 **Vietnam** — education named high-risk, `September 2027` horizon, instrument contested *(above)*.
🟢 **China** — the most binding framework: generative-AI service management measures and synthetic-content labelling rules effective `2025-09-01`.
🔵 **Singapore, Japan, Australia** — voluntary, principles-based, innovation-first. **ASEAN** published a Responsible AI Roadmap in 2025 running to 2030.
🔴 **No education-specific APAC adoption figure was found** — only cross-sector diffusion (Singapore `60.9%` among working-age adults; `1` in `10` APAC enterprises self-describing as *"very mature"*).
🟢 **The opportunity:** the spread from China's binding labelling rules to Australia's voluntary principles means a regional platform needs **per-jurisdiction policy nodes**, not one compliance mode — the shape p225's `P6` pattern already describes. 🟡 **This pass adds the reason it cannot be deferred: Korea's grace period expires inside the delivery window of anything started now.**

### 🟢 LATAM — the best-measured region on these shelves, and the gap is governance, not adoption

🟢 **UNESCO IESALC, `200` institutions across `19` countries: `87%` use AI in at least one area and `74%` in teaching and learning — against `26%` with a formal AI strategy.** 🔵 **Adoption is driven by individual academics, researchers and students rather than institutional plans.**

🔴 **No binding regional AI-in-education law surfaced.** Public-sector activity is capacity-building — UNESCO training for officials in Ecuador and the region.
🟢 **The opportunity, and it is the sharpest in any region:** a `61`-point gap between use and strategy *(`87%` vs `26%`)* is a **governance-retrofit** engagement on systems already in production. 🟡 **Not a build — an inventory, a policy, an evaluation record and an oversight design wrapped around tools faculty already adopted.** 🔵 **It is also the cheapest engagement to start, because the adoption that justifies it has already happened.**

🔴 **This pass's sources give `USD 7.52B` (2025) → `10.6B` (2026) → `42.48B` (2030) from one report, and `USD 12.3B` for 2026 from another attributing it to HolonIQ.** 🟡 **A `USD 1.7B` spread on the SAME year from two reports citing the same house.** 🔵 **Published as a conflict, not averaged** — the standing treatment on these shelves. 🟢 **The non-numeric global signals are more reliable and point one way: HolonIQ expects selective acceleration concentrated in course design, teacher productivity and admin workflow; 1EdTech reports institutions building governance structures and evaluation processes; and systems increasingly demand EVIDENCE that a product improves learning quality, persistence or job-relevant skills.**

revision and **rethinking assessment**. 🟢 A technical AI track enters the national
`bachillerato` from **`2026-27`**; a `2025` bill amending the General Education and General
Higher Education laws sat in the Education Committee as of May `2025`. 🟡 Press- and
communiqué-sourced; no DOF text reachable from this environment.

🆕 🟡 **Canada is a provincial patchwork, and that is the finding, not a gap.** 🔴 **There is no
federal instrument and CMEC is holding to provincial jurisdiction**, against pressure from the
Canadian Teachers' Federation for national guidance. 🟢 **British Columbia** publishes
*Considerations for Using AI Tools in K-12 Schools* — a decision framework, integration with
safeguards rather than restriction. 🟢 **Québec** updated its ministry guide on the *pedagogical,
ethical and legal* use of generative AI for **2026** (first issued `2024`), reportedly moving
from general caution to operational guidance on **assessment**, and refreshed its **Cadre de
référence de la compétence numérique on `21` April `2026`** with AI folded into the existing `12`
dimensions rather than bolted on; separate frameworks exist for cégeps and universities, **none
mandatory**. 🔴 **Sources disagree on the count** — three provincial ministries with published
K-12 guidance as of December `2025`, or four (Ontario, Québec, Alberta, BC); one source says
Ontario's ministry has issued no memorandum at all and the Ontario material is from the privacy
and human-rights commissioners. 🔴 **Flagged, not resolved.**

🔵 **Engagement shape:** a Canadian deal is **per-province**, and the artefact that travels is
the mapping between a tool's behaviour and each province's framework — BC's safeguards, Québec's
assessment rules. 🟢 **Québec is the one to lead with**: it has the most specific guidance and a
competence framework to map against.

🟡 **The United States remains the weakest-sourced cell on this page.** Secondary roundups report
only **`10`% of institutions** with formal AI guidelines against **`71`% of US teachers**
untrained, and a state-by-state patchwork (Colorado, Texas named). 🔴 **No primary federal or
state instrument was reachable this pass**, and `T207-12` records that the *"regulatory vacuum"*
framing is partly an artefact of pan-regional queries — the same framing hid Canada's and
Mexico's instruments until the organ was named. 🔵 **Run the organ sweep on US state education
agencies before quoting the vacuum to a client.**

### LATAM

🆕 🔴 **Brazil's binding instrument exists, is dated, and is one signature away.**
**`Parecer CNE/CP nº 15/2026`** was approved by the **Conselho Nacional de Educação on `1`
September `2026`**; its summary was published in the **`Diário Oficial da União` on `6` October
`2026`**; it now sits with **MEC for homologation, at which point it binds.**

🟢 **What it says, and it shapes product:** parameters for AI use **at every level and modality**
of teaching; AI **subordinated to educational purposes and student rights**; and AI **must not
replace education professionals**. 🔵 **p206 reported the binding instrument as *"in committee"*.
It has been approved for six weeks** — the cost of one unnamed organ.

🆕 🟡 **Four tracks, four timelines, and they are not coordinated.** A client asking *"what must
we comply with in Brazil"* has four answers:

| organ | instrument | date | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **CNE** *(council)* | `Parecer CNE/CP nº 15/2026` | approved `1` Sep `2026`, DOU `6` Oct `2026` | 🔴 **binds on homologation** |
| 🟡 **MEC** *(ministry)* | *Inteligência Artificial na Educação Básica* + the Segape referencial | April `2026` | 🟡 **orienting, not normative** |
| 🟡 **MEC + AGU** | Sandbox Regulatório de IA na educação | `24` March `2026` | 🟡 pilot; results feed future rules |
| 🟡 **Senado** *(legislature)* | `PL 2397/2026` — national ethical parameters for public **and private** institutions | introduced `14` May `2026` | 🔴 under deliberation |
| 🟢 **Paraná** *(state)* | first state technical AI course in the public network, `32` schools, ~`2 000` students | `2026` school year | 🟢 **running** |

🔵 **The product-shaping principles are stable across the ministry documents** — supervisão
humana, transparência, **student authorship**, `LGPD` + `ECA` — and AI is **not recommended in
`educação infantil`** except for inclusion. 🟡 **Reporting notes the early-childhood line is
guidance, not a national ban.** 🔴 All of it secondary: `gov.br` returns `000` from this
environment.

🟢 **The rest of the region, unchanged and worth restating against Brazil:** a UNESCO IESALC
study of `200` institutions across `19` countries finds **`87`% using AI in at least one area**
but only **`26`% with any formal framework**; a Digital Education Council survey reports **`92`%
of students and `79`% of faculty** actively using AI. 🔵 **Chile leads on national policy (AI
policy since `2021`, a bill in discussion); Brazil and Colombia have national strategies without
education-sector rules.** 🔴 **The regional constant is the same as Mexico's: use is near
universal, governance is not.**

🔵 **Engagement shape for LATAM:** the deliverable is the **governance layer**, and Brazil now
supplies its specification. 🟢 **Build to `CNE/CP 15/2026`'s three principles — subordination to
pedagogy, non-replacement of staff, student authorship — and the same artefact answers the
UNESCO `74`% who have no framework at all.**

### EMEA

🆕 🟡 **A second national AI-literacy mandate, dated `2027`.** France will make **one hour per
week of AI compulsory for all `seconde` students from the `2027` rentrée**, attached to the
existing **`SNT`** strand; announced June `2026`; the stated content is model mechanics, uses,
ethics, **digital sovereignty** and critical thinking against manipulation and disinformation.
🟡 Press-sourced, no ministry text reachable; teaching unions have raised timetable and
over-exposure concerns. 🔵 **An `18`-month runway is a dated buying window, and it is
teacher-facing: somebody has to train the teachers of every `seconde` class in France.**

🔴 **The regulatory clock is unchanged from `T206-8` and still the governing fact:** the EU
`Digital Omnibus` pushed **Annex III high-risk** systems to **`2` December `2027`**, while
**Article `50` transparency and Article `4` AI literacy are NOT delayed** and the **education
emotion-recognition ban has been in force since `2` February `2025`**. 🟢 **Annex III names
assessment, admissions and proctoring** — the three places an education product is most likely
to sit. 🔵 **Build switchable, not retrofittable.**

🟡 **Pan-regional EMEA enterprise sources remain unusable for education**: an explicit sweep
returned CompTIA, Workday and Bandwidth-Cavell material on enterprise AI adoption with **no
education-specific adoption statistic, ministry or vendor**. 🔴 **Written down rather than left
silent** — and `T207-1` says why, and what to do: **the EMEA cell will not fill from regional
queries. It fills one organ at a time** — France's `MEN`, Germany's `KMK` and the Länder, Spain's
`MEFP`, the Nordic agencies. 🟢 **Québec's and Brazil's cells both filled that way this pass.**

### APAC

🔴 **No new instrument this pass, and the pan-regional sweep failed the same way EMEA's did**:
enterprise AI governance material (Boomi, TechRepublic, Forrester sovereignty forecasts), plus
corporate skilling announcements — TCS × Pearson, LearnUpon's Sydney HQ, Alteryx Academy — and
**zero education-specific regulation or adoption statistics.** 🟢 **Recorded as an informed gap,
and it is the fourth region to confirm `T207-1`'s rule rather than an absence of policy.**

🟢 **What stands from p205 and p206, per country, which is how this cell was filled in the first
place:** **Singapore** made teacher AI-literacy module `1` **compulsory by end `2026`** — a dated
window, teacher-first. **South Korea's AI Basic Act entered force `22` January `2026`** and names
education *high-impact*; its mandatory AI textbooks reached **under `30`% adoption by March** and
were **stripped of official status by the National Assembly in August**. **China** mandates ≥`8`
h/yr with Beijing running `1 400`+ schools; **Japan's** MEXT Ver. `2.0` sits ahead of an FY`2030`
curriculum revision.

🔵 **The cross-regional pattern now has four data points and it is the most actionable thing on
this page:** 🟢 **mandates aimed at TEACHER capability survive — Singapore, and France's `2027`
curriculum hour is teacher-delivered.** 🔴 **Mandates aimed at CLASSROOM TOOLS do not — South
Korea's textbooks were withdrawn within seven months.** 🟢 **Sell the teacher-capability layer.
It is what survives a change of government, and it is what every one of these instruments is
reaching for.**

## Pass 206 — 2026-10-14 — `ACTION PJ` CLOSES ON LIMB `1`: BRAZIL'S POLICY WAS THERE ALL ALONG, IN PORTUGUESE

### 🟢 `ACTION PJ` — the hole was the query LANGUAGE, and the finding is large

🔴 **p205 ran an explicit Brazil query in English against *"LATAM"* and returned `0`
national-policy results**, and pre-registered two limbs: 🟢 limb `1`, a Portuguese query returns
dated national policy → **the hole was language**; 🔴 limb `2`, still nothing → **Brazil genuinely
has no national instrument**, which for the region's largest system would itself belong in every
LATAM deck.

🟢 **Limb `1` fires, and not marginally. The query `MEC inteligência artificial educação
diretrizes` returns four dated national instruments from 2026 alone:**

| date | instrument | binding? | what it covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| **março 2026** | **Referencial** on responsible AI use and development in education, from **Segape/MEC** | 🔴 **não normativo** | educação básica **and** superior, **including pós-graduação** |
| **março 2026** | **Sandbox Regulatório de IA**, MEC with the **AGU** | 🟡 experimental regime | testing AI systems inside a supervised regulatory environment |
| **8 abril 2026** | *"Inteligência Artificial na Educação Básica"* — documento orientador | 🔴 orientador | K-12 guidance for schools and teachers |
| **8 abril 2026** | *"IA na prática docente"* — teacher training course, **`5` modules** | — | fundamentals, technical aspects, ethical implications, pedagogical application |

🟢 **And the CNE is discussing *diretrizes nacionais* that WOULD bind** schools and universities.
🔵 **So Brazil's position is not "no instrument". It is "four instruments, none of them binding
yet, with the binding one in committee"** — a materially different thing to put in front of a
client, and the opposite of what an English-only channel reported for three passes.

🟢 **The principles, because they shape the product and not just the paperwork:** human
supervision; transparency about how the tool works; **analysis, synthesis and authorship must
remain the student's**; and alignment with **LGPD** and the **ECA** *(Estatuto da Criança e do
Adolescente)*. 🔴 **AI is NOT recommended in `educação infantil` at all, except where it enables
the inclusion of children with disabilities.** 🟢 **Higher education is told to stand up
governance guidelines and strengthen ethics committees, and to reform teacher-training degrees.**

🔵 **`ACTION PJ` and the licence-channel finding in [`agents/top.md`](../agents/top.md) are the
same fact.** 🔴 **The same English-only assumption hid Brazil's national AI-education policy from
the market channel AND hid two Brazilian school systems' `AGPL-3.0` grants from the licence
channel — found in one pass, on two instruments that share nothing but an alphabet.** 🟢 **p205's
rule *"per-country beats pan-regional"* now has a sibling: *per-language beats English-only*.**

## Opportunities by region

### North America

🟢 **Adoption is close to universal and policy is state-level, fragmented and fast-moving — the
combination that sells governance work.**

| fact | figure | note |
|---|---|---|
| university students using AI | **`92`%** | 2026 benchmark reporting |
| K-12 students using AI | **`54`%** | same source |
| education organisations using gen-AI | **`86`%** | 🔴 **most without a policy** — this gap IS the engagement |
| US states with K-12 AI guidance | 🟢 **over half**, by early 2026 | some now require **district-level** policies |

🟢 **Named instruments, each dated:** **Idaho SB 1227** — enacted; statewide framework, data
privacy rules, and **a bar on AI replacing human teachers**. **NYC Public Schools** — preliminary
guidance, **March 2026**, a traffic-light framework of permitted / cautioned / prohibited uses,
with a full playbook expected June 2026. **Katy ISD (Texas)** — generative-AI chatbots banned for
**K-6** from the 2026-27 year. **Arizona HB 4040** — 🟡 introduced, not enacted; would require AI
policies at K-12 **and public universities**. **Maryland** — 🟡 early-stage bills requiring the
State Department of Education to issue guidance and local systems to adopt policies.

🔴 **Federal law has not caught up.** The **K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
(H.R. 8747)** would let schools spend federal funds on AI curriculum and literacy; it **passed
committee on July 21, largely along party lines** — 🔴 **committee passage is not law.** 🔴 **One
source reports no binding federal AI curriculum standards as of May 2026.**

🔵 **The opportunity, concretely:** 🟢 **a district-policy-to-product pipeline.** `86`% deployed
against `~50`% of states with guidance and a traffic-light taxonomy already written in NYC means
the buyable artefact is **a configurable policy-enforcement layer over an existing LMS** — not a
tutor. 🟢 The permissive North American assets to build it on are on this KB's own shelf:
[`autolab/Autolab`](https://github.com/autolab/Autolab) (`Apache-2.0`, CMU),
[`Submitty/Submitty`](https://github.com/Submitty/Submitty) (`BSD-3-Clause`, RPI),
[`ucbds-infra/otter-grader`](https://github.com/ucbds-infra/otter-grader) (`BSD-3-Clause`, Berkeley)
and [`instructure/ims-lti`](https://github.com/instructure/ims-lti) (`MIT`) as the launch path.

🔴 **Declared gap, measured not assumed: `0` Canada and `0` Mexico results** in this pass's North
America sweep. 🔵 **Both are North America in this KB's closed vocabulary and both are unserved
here.** 🟢 **Next probe must be per-country and per-language** — the axis this pass established —
*not* another pan-regional English query, which has now failed twice.

### EMEA

🔴 **The high-risk deadline MOVED, and this is the pass that records the instrument.**

🟢 **The `Digital Omnibus` pushed stand-alone high-risk systems — which is where education sits,
under Annex III — to `2 December 2027`.** 🔴 **The sources disagree on the procedural history:**
one reports Council final approval on **29 June 2026** with the text still awaiting publication in
the Official Journal; another reports European Parliament approval on **16 June 2026**, pending
Council adoption. 🟡 **Both agree on the destination date. Neither is primary, and `eur-lex` is
`000` from here.**

🟢 **What is NOT delayed, and therefore binds now:**

| obligation | status | reach into education |
|---|---|---|
| **Article 50** transparency | 🟢 **not delayed — August 2026 applies** | a learner must be able to tell they are talking to a machine |
| **Article 4** AI literacy | 🟢 **in force** | 🔴 **staff who use AI must have sufficient literacy** — a training obligation, not a software one |
| **emotion recognition in education** | 🔴 **prohibited since `2 February 2025`** | medical / safety exception only |
| **Annex III high-risk** | 🟡 **`2 December 2027`** | admissions, assessing learning outcomes, monitoring students during tests |

🟢 **Annex III names the products:** automated essay grading, dropout prediction, exam proctoring.
🟢 **And pupils and parents can request an explanation of the system's role in a decision
affecting them**, once those provisions apply. 🔵 **That is an explainability requirement with a
named audience, and it is a build.**

🟢 **Named EMEA actors:** the European Commission's **AI Act Service Desk** *(which publishes
exam-proctoring examples)* and the **European AI Office**. 🔴 **Declared gap: `0` vendor
market-share or adoption-rate figures for EMEA returned this pass** — the channel gives
regulation, not a market map, and has now done so four passes running. 🔵 **Stop re-querying EMEA
regulation; p204 already declared that saturated and this pass re-confirms it.**

🔵 **The opportunity:** 🟢 **`14` months of runway is a product window, not a waiting period.**
Anything a studio ships into EMEA education between now and `2027-12-02` should be built so the
Annex III obligations can be switched on, not retrofitted. The permissive EMEA base exists:
[`ls1intum/Artemis`](https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis) (`MIT`, TU Munich, already carries
`gen-ai` and `text-exercises`) is the only major university-run platform on this shelf with a
permissive grant — 🔴 **[`INGInious/INGInious`](https://github.com/INGInious/INGInious) (UCLouvain)
is `AGPL-3.0`, which is network copyleft and a different conversation.**

### APAC

🟢 **The region splits cleanly into binding and voluntary, and 2026 moved one country across the
line.**

| country | instrument | status | education reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| **South Korea** | 🆕 **AI Basic Act** | 🟢 **in force `22 January 2026`** | 🔴 **names `education` explicitly as "high-impact AI"**, alongside healthcare, finance and employment |
| **China** | binding rules on algorithms, deep synthesis and generative AI; registration + penalties | 🟢 in force | AI **compulsory from age six** since September 2025 |
| **Japan** | voluntary, principles-based, enforced through existing sector law | 🟡 | 🟡 drafting a testing-and-assurance institute *(with Taiwan)* |
| **India** | 🔴 **no dedicated AI statute** | 🟡 **July 2026: government signalled it may pursue one**, on a risk-based model | adoption runs through edtech, not policy |

🆕 🔴 **The most useful APAC fact this pass is a failure, not a rollout.** 🟢 **South Korea's
mandatory AI textbooks were stripped of official status by the National Assembly in August**,
after adoption sat **below `30`% by March** and unions said the pace had outrun preparation.
🟡 **Single-sourced — flagged, not deck-ready** — but if it holds it is the strongest available
argument that **a mandate without teacher readiness fails**, from the country with the most
aggressive mandate in the region.

🟢 **India's demand is product-shaped, not policy-shaped:** AI used to **predict student
performance for early intervention**, with **Embibe** named. 🔵 **That is a dropout-prediction
build — the exact product Annex III classifies as high-risk in EMEA and that India does not yet
regulate.** 🔴 **A studio shipping one product into both markets is shipping into two different
legal regimes; design for the stricter one.**

🟢 **p205's per-country APAC findings stand unchanged** — China MoE's `≥8` hours of AI instruction
per year, Singapore's compulsory teacher AI-literacy module `1` by end `2026`, Japan's MEXT
guideline `Ver. 2.0`. 🔵 **This pass adds Korea's statute and the textbook reversal, and neither
was reachable from a pan-regional query.**

### LATAM

🟢 **Student adoption is the highest-confidence number in this whole file, and the policy picture
just changed shape — see `ACTION PJ` above.**

| fact | figure | source shape |
|---|---|---|
| LATAM higher-ed students using AI **regularly** | 🟢 **`92`%** | Digital Education Council 2026 survey, **`30 000`+ responses, `29`+ institutions** |
| using it **at least weekly** | 🟢 **`67`%** | same survey |

🟢 **General AI regulation, by country:** **Brazil** — `PL 2338/2023` approved by the Senado in
December 2024, 🔴 **still pending in the Câmara dos Deputados**. **Chile** — an AI bill in
*tramitación* on a risk-based, AI-Act-like model; 🟢 **data-protection law `21.719` enters force
`1 December 2026`**, which is the nearer and more concrete compliance date. **Mexico** — 🔴 the
*Ley Nahui* proposal is still in *trámite*; **no AI law.**

🟢 **`ILIA 2025` scores Brazil at `100` on the early-AI-education sub-indicator, shared with Chile,
Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic and Uruguay.** 🔴 **One secondary source attributes a binding
Chilean educational framework to a *"Ley 21.640 (2025)"* that no other source confirms and that
contradicts the reported status of Chile's AI bill.** 🔵 **Excluded. Do not put it in a deck.**

🟢 **A named edtech movement:** **Ignite Copilot** raised to expand AI solutions across
**Colombia, Mexico, Chile and Peru**, aimed at cutting administrative load and supporting
competency-based teaching. 🔵 **Administrative load, not tutoring — which matches what the
region's own open-source supply looks like.**

🔵 **The opportunity, and it is now specific:** 🟢 **Brazil's MEC referencial asks for exactly
three things a studio can build** — *human supervision in the loop*, *transparency about how the
tool works*, and *authorship kept with the student*. 🟢 **The LATAM-origin base to build on is
real and this pass re-read its grants first-hand:**
[`portabilis/i-diario`](https://github.com/portabilis/i-diario) and
[`portabilis/pre-matricula-digital`](https://github.com/portabilis/pre-matricula-digital) are
🔴 **`AGPL-3.0`** *(`35 326` B each, confirmed from the Portuguese body)* — 🔴 **network copyleft,
so a SaaS layer over them must be published**, which is a decision a client makes before the
build, not during it. 🔵 **The LGPD + ECA pairing in the referencial also means a Brazilian K-12
deployment carries a child-protection obligation that is NOT satisfied by GDPR-shaped controls.**

🔴 **Declared gap, measured:** 🟢 the only LATAM-origin *agent* the discovery channel surfaced this
pass, [`vitorr2101/Projeto-Agente-IA-Educacional`](https://github.com/vitorr2101/Projeto-Agente-IA-Educacional),
🔴 **carries no licence body at `7` path forms and therefore cannot be shipped.** 🔵 **The region's
usable supply is in the SCHOOL-SYSTEM tier (`AGPL`), not the agent tier.**

### Global

🔴 **The market-size figures did not improve and should still be quoted as a range with its
sources attached, never as a number:** Grand View ≈ **`$8.3`B (2025)** → **`$11.4`B (2026)**;

## Pass 205 — 2026-10-14 — `ACTION PF` CLOSED `3`/`3`: APAC'S GAP WAS THE QUERY SHAPE, NOT THE REGION

### 🟢 `ACTION PF` — per-country beats pan-regional, confirmed for a second time

🔴 **p204's pan-APAC sweep returned nothing on China, Singapore or Japan.** 🟢 **p205 asked the
three per-country queries the action registered. All `3` returned dated national policy —
limb `1` fires above its own `2`-of-`3` threshold, and `P521` is confirmed a second time.**
🔵 **The regional query shape was the defect. APAC's demand map is completable.**

## Opportunities by region

### North America

🟡 **The market figures diverge so widely they cannot be quoted as one number**, and this pass
adds a fourth reading rather than resolving them: MarketsandMarkets puts North America at
**`$951`M (2024) → `$2.3`B by 2029, `15.9`% CAGR**; Precedence gives the region **`38`% of global
share (2025)**; Technavio projects **`45`% CAGR 2025–2030** with higher education at **`$285.7`M
(2024)**. 🔴 **A `15.9`% and a `45`% CAGR cannot both describe the same market** — they scope
"AI in education" differently and none of the summaries states its scope. 🔵 **Use the regional
SHARE (`37`–`38`%, on which two independent houses agree) and refuse the growth rate.**

🟢 **The one procurement-grade datum found this window: Khanmigo district pricing at `$35` per
student per year.** 🔵 **That is a per-seat anchor a studio can actually build a business case
against** — a `10 000`-student district is a `$350`k/yr incumbent line, and an open-stack
alternative has to be priced against it, not against a market-size chart. 🔴 Secondary source;
verify before it reaches a proposal.

### EMEA

🔵 **The regulatory half was deliberately NOT re-searched this pass.** `ACTION NU-EU` retired it
after p204's fourth corroboration returned `0` new facts; re-running it is the known-cost mistake.
🟢 **Standing facts remain: Regulation (EU) `2026/1744`, OJ `2026-07-24`, in force `2026-07-27`;
Annex III education → `2027-12-02`; Annex I → `2028-08-02`; Art. `50` live `2026-08-02`;
Art. `50(2)` marking grace → `2026-12-02`.**

🟢 **The demand half was searched, and it yields a mechanism rather than a number:** university
LLM procurement in the EU is consolidating on **a unified contract layer** — one API and one
governance surface so an institution does not re-procure each time a model changes — routed
through **NREN and framework agreements**, with **HECVAT**, accessibility review, **DPIA** and
**FRIA** as named gates. 🔵 **`FRIA` (fundamental-rights impact assessment) is the one a studio
will be asked for and the one least likely to be in its template.**

🔴 **Declared gap, measured not assumed:** no EMEA-specific vendor market share, no per-country
university adoption rate, and no 2026 procurement volume were found. 🔵 **Next probe should be EU
tender databases (TED) or EDUCAUSE Europe, not another market-research summary** — the summaries
all resolve to the same global figure with no regional split.

### APAC

🟢 **China** — MoE guidelines (May 2025) put AI instruction in primary and secondary schooling
with **at least `8` hours of AI instruction per year**, standalone or embedded. Beijing: **`1 400`+
schools** in scope, a graded progression *(grade `3` basics → grade `4` data and coding → grade `5`
intelligent agents and algorithms → junior high machine-learning logic and misinformation
detection)*. 🔴 **Two hard guardrails: primary pupils may not use generative AI independently, and
teachers may not substitute AI for core instruction.** Sits inside the **2024–2035 education
Master Plan**. 🟡 Sources disagree on national reach *(nationwide vs Beijing-plus-pilots)* and on
school counts *(`1 400`+ vs `184` pilots)* — 🔵 **treat the `8`-hour floor and the Beijing
progression as solid, the national framing as unconfirmed.**

🟢 **Singapore — the most procurement-relevant finding in the region.** MOE's **Teacher AI
Literacy Professional Learning Roadmap** makes **module `1` COMPULSORY for all primary, secondary
and JC teachers, due end `2026`**; modules `2`–`3` encouraged by end `2027`; subject-specific
advanced courses from `2027`. 🔴 **That is a dated, mandatory, nationwide teacher-training
obligation with a deadline `~7` weeks out** — 🟢 **a named buying window for exactly the

teacher supervision. 🔴 **One claim found and NOT confirmed:** a blog reports a May 2026
announcement making baseline AI modules compulsory across all tertiary courses by 2027; 🔵 no MOE

🟢 **Japan** — MEXT's *"Guideline for the Use of Generative AI in Elementary and Secondary
Education"*, **Ver. `2.0`, dated December 2024**, re-posted March 2026. Four pillars: safe use,
information security, protection of personal data/privacy/copyright, fairness. 🔴 **Inappropriate

🔵 **So Japan is a slow, documented, standards-led market: the money is in compliance-shaped
teacher tooling, not in student-facing chat.**

### North America

## Pass 200 — 2026-10-14 — MARKET SNAPSHOT

🔵 **p199's framing — *"the spread is the finding, not the midpoint"* — survives this pass and
is reinforced.** Searched again, the figures on offer are: **$10.6B (2026) → $42.48B (2030)**
(Research and Markets); **~$32B by 2030** (a K-12 sector report); and **$12.3B for 2026**
attributed to HolonIQ **but cited secondhand by a vendor blog**. 🔴 **Three "2026 market sizes"
spanning $10.6B–$12.3B and two different 2030 endpoints that differ by `$10B`.** 🟢 **Do not put
a single number in a client deck. Put the range and the disagreement** — the disagreement is
the more defensible statement and it is the honest one.

### 🔴 The regional figures are aggregator-grade, and that is load-bearing

This pass found regional market sizes for the first time: **North America `36%` share, $3.68B
(2026) → $32B (2030)**; **Europe $2.64B (2026) → $8.0B (2030) at `31.9%` CAGR.** 🔴 **Both come
from statistics-roundup sites, not from the research houses themselves**, and the North America
2030 figure *equals* the K-12 report's figure for the **whole world**. 🔵 **At least one of
those two is wrong, and a reader cannot tell which from the sources available.** 🟢 **Use them
for shape — North America is roughly a third of the market, Europe roughly a fifth — and never
as a quotable figure.**

### 🟢 The one adoption statistic worth building a pitch on, and it is LATAM's

**UNESCO IESALC with UNU-IAS surveyed `200` institutions across `19` countries** in Latin
America and the Caribbean:

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| institutions using AI in **at least one** area | 🟢 **`87%`** |
| using it in **teaching and learning** | **`74%`** |
| 🔴 institutions with a **formal AI strategy** | 🔴 **`26%`** |

🔵 And the report's own explanation of the gap: adoption *"is often driven by individual
academics, researchers, and students rather than institution-wide strategies."*

🟢 **That `87` / `26` gap is the clearest engagement thesis in this entire KB**, for three
reasons: it is a named institutional sample rather than a vendor panel; the gap is *governance*,
which is institution-level work a studio sells rather than a tool a vendor sells; and **the same
shape is independently visible in EMEA** — one roundup reports **only `10%` of `450+` surveyed
institutions have formal AI guidelines.** 🔵 A separate Digital Education Council LATAM survey
(`29` institutions) adds the depth dimension: **`92%` of students and `79%` of faculty engage
with AI, but `88%` of faculty report only "minimal" to "moderate" engagement** — wide, and
shallow.
